📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perez Hilton has returned to his Miami residence after a health incident left him hospitalized.

The 48-year-old was hospitalized in August following a distressing livestream that prompted several calls to police and requests for a welfare check.

Officers ultimately transported Hilton to a nearby hospital, while mental health professionals and the Crisis Response Unit offered support to his friends and family.

Recent findings suggest that hilton received treatment for multiple broken bones and significant blood loss. After undergoing surgery, he was transferred to an inpatient medical facility.

Now, his family has revealed that Hilton is “back with his family while continuing his recovery through an intensive outpatient program.”.

They noted that he is getting "ongoing therapy" and "mental health support.".

Recent findings suggest that “Over the past few weeks, Perez has enjoyed several successful weekend visits with his mom and children. Being reunited with his loved ones has meant so much to everyone, especially after these past few difficult months. With Thanksgiving approaching, we’re looking forward to spending some much-needed quality time together as a family and enjoying a little peace and quiet during the holiday," the statement continued.

In September, his family shared an upgrade on the situation as they begged fans to vacate his property.

The message revealed that before the livestream event, Hilton's "children, niece, and sister were inside the home.".

"When it became clear that Perez was experiencing a severe mental health crisis and harming himself, they immediately fled to protect the children from witnessing any further trauma," the message continued.

The patch stated the family's priority was "helping the children begin to heal from what they experienced," while explaining that allowing them to return to the privacy and familiarity of their home is an notable part of that process.

Hilton's family previously revealed that he was receiving medical care and was "able to communicate.".

The update came after Hilton opened about his move to Realtor.com®, reflecting on what he'll miss most about his property and his fond memories of Las Vegas.

“It is a beautiful home, and it served me well personally and professionally," he said. "I filmed tons of television segments and news interviews from this home, and produced two documentaries.

In a recent development, "I would film every day for my socials, and livestream as well, and I do a lot of talking head commentary work. I filmed tons of specials for different networks and streamers in my home and outdoors. It's just so beautiful,".

"All three of my favorite spaces in the home have one thing in common—they are all very healing for me. The primary bath has the biggest, most luxurious shower that I've ever had, and the closet is huge and has so much space. Also, I never had my own, dedicated office before, and I really loved that. It's just the perfect home for a family. Everybody has space," he added.

Industry observers note that speaking about the property's location, Hilton told Realtor.com, "It was vital for me to be close to the Strip, but it’s equal distance to Summerlin and everywhere we needed to be. My children’s schools, doctors, and dentists were all just a few minutes away.”.

Hilton was especially pleased with the fact that his mother had her own private living space. One of home designer Blue Heron's signature features is a "NexGen Suite," and, because he bought the home before it was finished, he got to customize elements of the layout to ensure they were perfect for his mom.

“This was perfect for me, because my mother is a huge part of my family,” said Hilton. “She’s both grandmother and co-parent to my children. To be able to give her the space that she deserves was notable. She had her own entrance, her own living room and kitchenette area.".

However, despite his love for Nevada, Hilton noted that he is confident in his decision.

"It just feels like the right move, the only move, to make at this time. I've loved Las Vegas, but it's time to be closer to family," he added.

In a recent development, the property is being sold with Kathryn Winterton of Las Vegas Sotheby’s real estate agency, who told Realtor.com, "This home was designed for the way people want to live and entertain today. The natural light, open spaces, and seamless connection to the backyard create an atmosphere that feels both sophisticated and welcoming.".

The home spans 7,000 square feet and boasts several modern living spaces, as well as a resort-style pool.

As in so many family dwellings, Hilton says the kitchen is the heart of the home, with its premium appliances, sleek custom cabinetry and a massive dining and prep island.

The kitchen opens up to the high-ceiling living and dining areas, which feel expansive, welcoming and luxurious. Generous walls of glass provide abundant natural light create a light, airy atmosphere.

It has been revealed that outdoors on the acre lot there's a pool, spa, lush landscaping and multiple outdoor gathering spaces. Hilton said he did a lot of his production work outside, as there are a variety of luxurious backdrops ideal for his commentary.

Set in a chic, private gated neighborhood known as Prado, Hilton enjoyed the fact that the home is on a corner lot in a small community with fewer than 20 homes.

Hilton and his family enjoyed the home, the community and Las Vegas in general so much he states he feels a bit of guilt moving his family away. But "kids are adaptable," he says. He knows this from experience.

A little over three years ago, Hilton packed up his three children and his mother and moved to Las Vegas from Los Angeles, the city where he had infinite Hollywood connections and a luxe, six bedroom, five bath classic Spanish Colonial built in 1926.

Prior to that, Hilton and his family lived in New York City for several years.

Hilton took to Instagram to explain the reasoning behind his move from Las Vegas, where he has been living for the past 3.5 years.

Recent findings suggest that "We’re moving permanently to Miami. I am so excited, not nervous. I know this is the right move for me and my children and my mother," he said at the beginning of the video.

Although Hilton insisted he has "nothing but wonderful memories" while calling Nevada home, he claimed that his decision to relocate to the Sunshine State came from a higher power.

In a recent development, “I need to move to Miami for many reasons. First, this is heaven-sent. God told me to move to Miami. ... The holy spirit made these words come out of my mouth: ‘Let’s move to Miami,'" he noted.

The influencer noted that his "trauma" from growing up in The Magic City has since been "released.".

“My entire family is in Miami. I still have friends from high school. Though I have not lived there in 30 years, it has always been my home. Once we move there, any second now, it will feel like home right away," he added.

Hilton, who has three children via surrogacy, said a large part of his decision to move was due to his difficult year, which was filled with several health scares, including a 21-day hospital stay and a blood clot.

Recent findings suggest that "Even though it was really painful being in the hospital and so sick, I reconnected with my faith, and this move to Miami feels divine. I was just listening to God. I used to not have a great relationship with Miami when I was younger, but now things are different and Miami is different, and I'm excited to get to rediscover it as an adult," he told Realtor.com.

Speaking about his health woes, he mentioned, "I know this move will be great for my family. Nearly dying this year twice and the experience here—you never think it’s going to happen, but it was just so hard not only for me but my mom, for the kids, for my sister who is in Los Angeles. Everybody else is in Miami. To a new beginning and thank you, God, for guiding me back to Florida where my family needs to be.”.

Despite the market downturn, XRP Ledger is showing a somewhat reassuring trend: the price has bounced toward the $1 mark and, thankfully, the move is followed by a volume uptick, which could start a proper recovery rally.

XRP is trading at $0.96 after dipping to $0.89. The $1 threshold, which essentially enables a rapid decrease if broken, gave in on November 14. It's the first time XRP traded below $1 since mid-August.

The market is bearish, and the RSI dropped into the 20-ish zone, which is considered "extremely oversold". Moving averages are still rapidly diverging, which might further reinforce the bearish dynamic.

Even if XRP reclaims the round number, bulls might still stay sidelined. If bulls somehow wake up, a recovery toward $1.2 is the main priority, as it's the level where a lot of investors accumulated XRP in the past.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, the Ledger shows elevated activity, with the potential to go further and reclaim levels we haven't seen in the bear market. Still, elevated activity during a prolonged market descent is not something we should just shake off.

According to on-chain data, payment volume on the XRP Ledger reached around 1.1 billion XRP, up 139.9%. Active accounts went up by 154.5%, reaching 42,300. Payments volume growth is substantial, but not record-breaking by any means.

It has been revealed that the XRP Ledger has seen substantial growth in various on-chain metrics, which, unfortunately, does not give the price enough support. A lot of the Ledger activity might be automated, driven by either trading bots or sophisticated LLM models. The market is mostly driven by speculative interest rather than fundamental network usage.

The activity of investors who are trying to cash out or pull their holdings away from exchanges could be the key here. Growing payments volume most likely reflects growing fear among investors, as some of them move funds to exchanges in order to liquidate their coins.

Payments volume rises, but so does the bear market pressure, with a possibility of a further downturn that could make things worse than they already are.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Engel & Völkers announced an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.
  • Industry observers note that brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into upcoming markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies.
  • eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engel & Völkers announced an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.

Industry observers note that brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into upcoming markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it plans to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. IRES MLS welcomed back a former staffer to run operations, and Howard Hanna Portside added an agent in Massachusetts.

Industry observers note that engel & Völkers expanded into Aruba with license partners Zobaida Akkari and Richard Franken, Aruba-based entrepreneurs with backgrounds in real estate, luxury sales, hospitality and tourism. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the company.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, remarked in a statement.

Realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the firm. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, claims it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa remarked in a statement.

According to recent reports, rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the manufacturer.

Jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

Industry observers note that baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen remarked in a statement.

According to recent reports, dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

“Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs said in a statement.

IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl said in a statement.

According to recent reports, howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the company.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter said in a statement.

At press time, Bitcoin is trading at $65,450, according to TradingView. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Nov. 13, and it dropped below $67,000 over the weekend.

The AI tech giant is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each and aims to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee called the current drawdown a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, as investors sell liquid assets to buy shares in the largest offerings of the year.

According to recent reports, after SpaceX started trading on Nasdaq, the price of Bitcoin kept falling for another 18 days. After that, Bitcoin went up, and 100 days after the IPO, it was 28% above its close on the day of the listing.

If Bitcoin repeats this pattern after the Anthropic IPO, it could reach $90,000 by the end of February 2027, according to Strive CEO Matt Cole.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared the comparison of the two charts on X and called Cole's numbers "an interesting analysis." Still, some users in the replies under the post blamed the drop of Bitcoin on selling by Binance, not on the IPO calendar.

The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.
  • According to recent reports, many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home.
  • Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.

According to recent reports, many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home. But that's not necessarily true.

Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.

Recent findings suggest that these programs can help buyers snag a home by providing cash that can go toward a down payment. There are even loan programs for certain qualified buyers that don't require any down payments. The array of offerings from federal, local, and private sources can take the form of looser loan requirements, outright grants of money, or tax credits, all of which make homeownership more affordable.

According to recent reports, first-time homebuyers, often with certain qualifications, are often beneficiaries of the assistance. Lower-income buyers, those who serve in the military or are veterans, and those who purchase fixer-uppers or homes in rural areas might also be eligible for the help.

The assistance ranges greatly, from a grant of several thousand dollars to, at the high end, a savings of five figures over the life of the loan.

Down payment assistance can take several forms and can even help buyers circumvent the PMI payment.

While 20% down has been something of a gold standard for homebuyers, it's also the minimum that generally lets them avoid private mortgage insurance, or PMI, which is assessed because lenders believe the loan carries risk. This in turn raises the homebuyer’s monthly expenses.

Here's an example: PMI is typically 0.5% to 1% of the loan amount per year. So if buyers put down less than 20% and their mortgage is $300,000, their PMI would be between $1,500 and $3,000 per year. That would add about $125 to $250 per month on top of their mortgage payment, a significant charge. (Homeowners can have PMI canceled when the equity in their home surpasses 20%.).

So, while a buyer can also choose loans that require a down payment of just a single digit, that PMI can stretch a budget paper-thin. That's where down payment assistance can help.

Recent findings suggest that at least 2,000 such programs exist across the country. Some are federal, but most tend to be at state and local levels, which is vital to know when searching for help. Private organizations, from lenders to nonprofits, also work with borrowers who need help.

In a recent development, these programs might offer grants, loans, tax credits, or a combination of a couple of these benefits. Funding can come from our government, nonprofits, and private enterprises. Let’s take a closer look:.

Grants might be the most desirable form of down payment assistance. Typically, a grant is fully forgiven at closing and never has to be paid back. Yes, we’re talking about free money!

In a recent development, about 7% of down payment help comes in the form of grants, says Veronica Khandelwal, vice president of HFA Relations at Down Payment Resource, which provides consumers with guidance on this kind of assistance. But there is a catch.

It has been revealed that “Grants require owner occupancy," she indicates of the requirement for buyers to live in these properties. That's to make sure these loans don't go to investors or vacation-home buyers. "Some programs allow grants to be applied to multifamily purchases of one to four units so long as one of the units is occupied by the borrower.".

Forgivable loans are another option. These loans need to be repaid only if a repayment trigger event occurs, such as the home being sold before the end of the term, the home being no longer owner-occupied, the title being transferred, or the loan being defaulted on.

Industry observers note that deferred-payment loans are also available. These are paid back either at the end of the loan term or if a repayment trigger occurs. So, while it’s not a gift, it will help homebuyers get over that down payment hurdle and buy a house they might otherwise not have been able to afford.

Sources indicate that repayable loans are another leg up on homeownership. They require borrowers to make monthly payments, like a typical loan. But here's the good part: They do so at interest rates starting as low as 0%. That helps spread the down payment and closing costs over a number of years, making it much easier to enter the housing market.

Some agencies also offer a combination of these forms of assistance. That could mean that a portion of the help will be forgiven (or “written off” with no repayment needed), while some will need to be repaid. Tax credits are sometimes offered as well, further sweetening the deal.

Each down payment assistance program will have its own rules and guidelines, but the vast majority are offered only for a home that buyers will live in as a primary residence.

Here are some of the more popular national options folks might access to help them to pivot from home shopper to homebuyer.

Industry observers note that FHA (Federal Housing Authority) loans were created by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for first-time homeowners (HUD). These mortgages allow as little as 3.5% for the down payment, provided buyers have a credit score of 580 or higher, along with other qualifying factors. The federal government insures these loans, and for that reason, banks are more willing to loan money to homebuyers who have neither top-tier credit nor loads of cash to put down on the purchase.

FHA Section 203(k) loans require only 3% down, provided qualifying buyers will live in the property, typically one that needs work, while they fix it up. For buyers hoping for a DIY route into a dream home, this could be a win-win. The cost of improvements is included in the loan so buyers can finance both the home and up to $35,000 in repairs.

But buyers beware: The cost of materials and construction labor has spiked since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and work is taking much longer to be completed than ever before.

Sources indicate that VA (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) loans might be offered directly by the VA or backed by the department. Several factors are considered, such as service history, duty status, income, and credit rating. But those who qualify can purchase a home with zero down as long as the sales price isn’t higher than the home’s appraised value.

Industry observers note that fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are federally funded loans that can help buyers skirt steep down payments. The Home Possible, HomeReady, and HomeOne loans typically offer a 3% down payment mortgage to qualifying, lower-income homebuyers.

Good Neighbor Next Door is another HUD-sponsored program. In this case, law enforcement officers, teachers, firefighters, and emergency medical technicians can enjoy a substantial incentive in the form of a discount of 50% from the list price of the home in a community that is being revitalized. The buyer must live in the house for three years as a primary residence.

Teacher Next Door Grant is a program similar to the one above but is designed to help educators own their own homes. Grants to the tune of up to $8,000 in certain areas are possible with additional down payment assistance available in some circumstances.

Sources indicate that the USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) Rural Home Loan Program was created to assist people buying homes in rural locations. For qualifying, single-family properties, loans might be available with no money down. There are maximum income limits and other qualifications to be eligible for one of these mortgages.

There are plenty of other programs available as well. Different states and cities, as well as individual lenders and nonprofits, can help prospective homebuyers get the financing they need. Folks should put their location and "down payment assistance" into a search engine, and take a look at what's available. They might see everything from Habitat for Humanity to local religious organizations pop up. Also,visit Down Payment Resource.

Sources indicate that one other path to explore is whether a buyer's job provides down payment assistance. A lot of employers may offer assistance in  the form of a $10,000 loan that is forgivable after five years.

Down payments hit a four-year low at the start of 2026. The median payment fell to $23,400 and 12.8% in Q1 2026, down 19% and 1.2 ppts year over year.

However, down payments remain well above pre-pandemic levels, as more buying is happening in the lower-down-payment South and Midwest, even as the Northeast stays deeply competitive.

It has been revealed that the Northeast posted the highest median down payment at $57,600, reflecting higher home prices and more competition. The Northeast also sees the largest gap between what buyers are paying as a down payment today compared to pre-pandemic.

Industry observers note that compared to 2019, the Northeast has seen down payments climb 236.8%, significantly more than the next closest gap of 134.0% in the Midwest. These trends are consistent with the persistent upward pressure on home prices in these regions as scarce inventory is met with sustained buyer demand.

Get ready for some good news. There are a lot of misconceptions about who qualifies for down payment assistance.

“Many people think these programs are only available to low-income borrowers, first-time homebuyers, or for properties that have sales price limits,” says Down Payment Resource's Khandelwal. “But if you look, you’ll find specialized programs designed to assist specific groups, including first-generation homebuyers, minorities, Indigenous people, people of color, veterans, those with government jobs, disabilities, and more.”.

Here’s something else to smile about: A first-time homebuyer doesn't just mean someone who's never bought a home before.

Sources indicate that the federal government generally holds a broader definition of a first-time homebuyer. It’s someone who has not been a homeowner in the past three years. If you sold a house three-and-a-half years ago, you qualify as first-time buyer.

Buyers can take several different steps to find a down payment assistance program that’s right for them.

Check the federal programs mentioned above (like HUD, VA, USDA, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac), and see if there’s anything suitable.

Buyers should also visit their state’s Department of Housing website and see what might be listed, or call their number and inquire what down payment assistance programs might be available. Cities, towns, private lenders, and nonprofits may also have help.

“Homebuyers should seek the assistance of a mortgage lender who specializes in affordable lending to identify their best options,” advises Khandelwal.

In terms of what is typically needed to access aid, the documentation is very much in line with what’s needed to apply for any mortgage. Buyers will likely need the following:.

Pay stubs plus W-2s from the past few years to verify employment and income history.

Any 1099 forms showing other income.

Details on the property they intend to buy (The real estate agent can share this information.).

The paperwork is processed in much the same way as a home loan, and there may be requests for more documents.

Then, if buyers are approved, they will be ready to move ahead with a lower—or no—down payment as their homeownership journey unfolds.

Janet Siroto is a journalist, editor, and trend tracker. Her work has appeared in Cosmopolitan, Good Housekeeping, and other publications.

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

It’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

To leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

Season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

At the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio said the injury took two or three months to heal.

The following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He said he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

Recent findings suggest that I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. Industry observers note that actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a major, big fight. Industry observers note that according to CoinGlass, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on the Coinbase spot market reached -$1.08 billion between Oct. 31 and Nov. 15. CVD reveals the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

Sources indicate that the price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

Recent findings suggest that the data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some users on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that showed client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several users in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

Sources indicate that coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

Sources indicate that anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

The CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.

In a recent development, onchain data platform CoinGlass seeks to answer why XRP's price is down. Its analysis, generated from the past 24 hours of futures, spot and ETF data, points to three indicators that help explain the pressure on XRP.

Industry observers note that first is a 'long squeeze,' which increased selling pressure on the price. Long traders have taken the biggest hit during the latest decline. CoinGlass data shows that XRP long liquidations reached $43.17 million over the past 24 hours, accounting for about 91% of total liquidations.

In a recent development, second, open interest has fallen as traders, largely longs, close positions. XRP open interest has fallen 5.53% in the past 24 hours to $2.03 billion.

Thirdly, XRP is currently in negative funding at -0.0082%. Negative funding in perpetual futures markets means that short sellers are paying long sellers to keep positions open, a sign traders are bearish on the market.

In a recent development, XRP fell for 10 straight days from November 5 to November 14, 2026. Price lost momentum after losing the daily MA 200 at the close of October. The cryptocurrency lost another crucial support in early October, the daily MA 50, weakening bulls.

In a recent development, stablecoin supply is shrinking fast, dropping $17 billion over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022. As holders swap stablecoins to fiat, they drain buying power from BTC and crypto, analysts at Glassnode said.

It will be watched if buying power returns to the market; according to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a big buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when.".

Sources indicate that the daily RSI has entered oversold levels, with the possibility of a relief rally in the coming session. Such a recovery, if sustained, will target the daily MA 50 and 200 at $1.25 and $1.30. Further downside is expected to find support at $0.77.

Elle and Dakota Fanning have been in the spotlight for decades, but their upcoming project, “The Nightingale,” marks the first time they’ve played sisters onscreen—an experience that brought them “closer” together, both on set and at home.

While they’ve visited each other on set in the past and even separately played different versions of the same character in the 2001 film “I Am Sam,” Elle, 28, told Vanity Fair that actually working with each other is a totally different ball game.

In a recent development, “It certainly brought us closer, which was hard to imagine—to be closer,” she said. “Our mom always left us little notes in suitcases, like, ‘Just savor this time together. This is precious.’”.

Dakota, 32, confirmed that they took their mother’s advice.

It has been revealed that “We did really savor it,” she mentioned. “And the biggest takeaway for me is when we have each other and when we’re together, we can do anything. That’s really how I feel. There’s nothing that I couldn’t do with Elle there with me.”.

Sources indicate that that remarked, the job wasn’t easy. The Fannings traveled to Budapest to shoot on location, where they lived together.

“It was a challenging shoot, not going to lie. It was physically tiring, certainly emotionally taxing,” said Elle.

After a long day of using lots of “brain power” on set, the sisters had to find a way to “recharge” each evening.

For Dakota and Elle, that meant eating lots of Thai food and streaming “The Real Housewives,” true crime, and “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”—the TV series the younger sister stars in, which was released while they filmed “The Nightingale.”.

Dakota revealed that on a day off, she’d often find herself cleaning up after Elle, which was poetic as her character, Vianne, also tidies her sister Isabelle’s mess.

“Her bed in the mornings is like a tornado has run through it,” she mentioned. “She’s just one of those sleepers. It’s all twisted into a crazy thing. I was like, ‘That’s no fun to get into a bed that’s all crumpled and rumpled. Let me make it nice.’”.

The older sister mentioned that “it became a routine,” and she “always made her bed like that” when possible.

Elle stated, “It’s art imitating life, because there’s even a scene where Vianne is making Isabelle’s bed, too.”.

It has been revealed that dakota and Elle were born in Conyers, GA. As young girls, they traveled between the Atlanta suburb and Los Angeles to work before relocating to the West Coast full time.

Sources indicate that “When we were younger, we wanted to make sure that people saw us differently, and we wanted to give each other space to carve our own path,” Elle told Vanity Fair in 2025. “But as adults, it’s been very fulfilling to merge.”.

One of the most major ways the sisters have merged their lives in adulthood was in 2017, when they purchased a gorgeous $2.3 million property together.

According to Architectural Digest, they lived in a Cape Cod-style home in the Valley Village area of San Fernando Valley.

The 4,550-square-foot residence was perched at the end of a private, gated driveway and had a very classic aesthetic with white rose bushes planted along the front walkway.

The interiors were defined by delicate details, such as baby blue brocade-patterned walls, intricate chandeliers, and coffered ceilings.

The sisters sold the six-bedroom, six-bathroom estate for just under $2.7 million in May 2020.

It’s clear that Dakota was a fan of the dwelling’s traditional style, as she bought a very similar-looking home in Toluca Lake for $2.95 million in 2019, just before offloading the property she shared with Elle.

According to Architectural Digest, Dakota’s newer home spans 4,428 square feet and boasts five bedrooms and six bathrooms. It’s flooded with natural light and, like the first home, has crystal chandeliers, a pool in the backyard, and a double-height entry hall.

#6643. We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople.
  • It has been revealed that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since.
  • In a recent development, you didn’t fail the program.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople. Learn what to ask before you pay for a coaching program.

It has been revealed that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since. I’ve also sold the thing I’m about to take apart, so keep that in mind while you read.

In a recent development, you didn’t fail the program. The program failed you. How come?

According to recent reports, the reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be. Nearly every coaching program in this business teaches professional sales skills to people who are not in sales. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators.

Industry observers note that nobody has ever talked a family into a house they didn’t want to live in. What we do is help people through the largest and most emotional decision of their lives with the least amount of damage. We read a room. We tell someone the truth about their kitchen, and we hold a deal together at 9 p.m. on a Sunday when the buyer’s father has opinions.

According to recent reports, that is not selling. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators. If you can fog a mirror, you can get a license. Very few people can do those four things well, and I’ve yet to see a program that teaches them as a skill set.

According to recent reports, this isn’t the coach’s fault. Coaches were trained the same way the rest of us were. Build the database. Reach as many people as you possibly can. Add value, and then add more of it tomorrow.

According to recent reports, there’s a word buried in there that I think is the dumbest one in our industry, and I say that with love. Value.

We all have the same value. Every one of us can pull a comp, open a door, write an offer and get to a closing table. What almost none of us have is a point of differentiation, the thing that tells a consumer specifically what you do for them and why it ought to be you. You can follow “add value” for a decade and stay interchangeable with the other four agents the seller interviewed.

There’s a second reason the homework never gets done: Agents live in two periods of time: now and not now.

Now is the pipe that burst three hours before a closing. Now is the appraisal, the inspection, the client calling at 10:30 p.m. about something that could have been a text. Now is loud, it’s permanent, and it pays this month. Not now is quiet and pays in three years, if at all.

In a recent development, the trouble is that everything producing long-term income security in this business sits in the not-now column. The National Association of Realtors’ 2026 member profile puts median gross income at $88,500 for agents with 16 years or more in the industry, and $8,000 for agents with two years or less.

Sources indicate that the veterans report a median 49 percent of their business from repeat clients and another 32 percent from referrals. For the newest agents, both of those medians are zero.

Somebody will say that’s just arithmetic, that you need a past client before you can have a repeat one. That’s the point. The whole gap is 15 years of relationships, and not one hour of that work feels urgent on a Tuesday. This is a patient business being coached like an impatient one.

Industry observers note that we do something else I think is worse. We coach in a permanent state of enthusiasm. Everything is fabulous; every market is an opportunity; you’re crushing it; this is your year. I call that toxic positivity, and it does real damage. You sit in a hard month with two deals coming apart, you hear all of it, and you quietly conclude the problem must be you.

Industry observers note that what would help is unglamorous. This job burns through five things: prioritization, organization, time management, impulse control and emotional regulation. By Thursday of an ordinary week, most good agents are running low on at least two.

According to recent reports, there’s nothing wrong with any of those people. Real support builds bumpers around those five, the same reason a bowling lane for kids has them. You don’t make the gutter disappear by concentrating harder.

In a recent development, that work means dealing with people as they are, for who they are. Not more, more, more. Not the next great thing. One thing, chosen for that person, small enough to start on a Thursday when everything else has gone sideways.

We haven’t served this business well on that, and I include myself. I’ve sold the four-week cycle. It’s a comfortable thing to sell, because Week 1 always works.

According to recent reports, if you’re picking a program this fall, ask what gets cut. Anybody can hand you 15 things. The one worth paying is the person who tells you which one matters and which 14 you can skip.

Industry observers note that we’re not in sales. We never were. Until the coaching in this business is built for that job, we’ll keep running very good people through programs that leave them feeling like the problem.

Recent findings suggest that you aren’t the problem. This is still the best time there’s ever been to be a great agent. We just have to stop training you for somebody else’s job.

The views and opinions expressed here are those of the contributor and separate from the Inman newsroom.

Sources indicate that lance Pendleton is the founder of Reframe Lab, a coaching and consulting practice for real estate agents, and the former national head of agent development at Compass in Connecticut. Get connected on Instagram.

The salon owner’s home—which viewers will recognize from the reality series—is a sprawling hillside estate that has been on and off the market for the past two years.

The four-bedroom, three-bathroom modern abode was first listed for $4.5 million in September 2024. The price was decreased to $4.38 million in March 2025, then to $3.85 million just two months later.

By December of last year, the listing was removed. It hit the market again in January 2026 for $3.85 million, where it sat for most of the year before being removed on Oct. 14.

In a recent development, the couple purchased the 6,369-square-foot residence for an undisclosed sum in 2020. With soaring ceilings, white ash floors, and lots of sleek, marble surfaces, the modern abode has a distinct luxurious aesthetic.

In addition to the chic white minimalist space at the center of the home, a concealed catering kitchen is equipped with Miele appliances, a separate refrigerator and freezer, and a space for staff to prepare food.

According to recent reports, it seems as if, despite the separation, daily life hasn’t changed too much in the home. Katsanevas noted that Trujillo stops by most days to pick up their 15-year-old daughter, Elektra, and take her to school.

“He’ll come in and have coffee,” she explained. “He’ll bring her home from lessons, and we’ll have dinner together. We are still just spending time together. We’re best friends. We are peaceful, it’s positive. We have a lot to do together.”.

She noted that Trujillo remains close with her father and will celebrate the holidays with the family.

“My dad sends him all of his favorite dishes and continues to cook for him,” remarked Katsanevas. “Shawn will spend Thanksgiving and Christmas with my family.”.

Although they are still connected in many ways, Katsanevas noted that after nearly three decades together, “space and doing things independently” have brought clarity.

It has been revealed that “We are even going to different churches now,” she shared. “And that’s huge for me. We started out going to the same church.”.

Katsanevas and Trujillo currently operate nine locations of their business, Lunatic Fringe Salon, across Utah, Ohio, and Idaho.

While she’s focused on remaining positive, Katsanevas said it took some time to work through the complicated feelings that accompanied the change.

Pancake now operates across more than 11 blockchain networks. The platform reports over 208 million owners and more than $4.4 trillion in cumulative trading volume.

In a recent development, its services now include perpetual contracts, tokenized stocks, ETFs, yield products, and developer infrastructure. The project is also preparing a dedicated mobile application. Its CAKE ticker and contract address remain unchanged, with existing staking positions unaffected.

Pancake’s relationship with Binance makes this rebrand interesting. Binance Labs announced a strategic investment in CAKE in June 2022. The investment supported the decentralized exchange’s development within the BNB Chain ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the rivalry becomes clearer when looking beyond the latest announcements. Binance has already introduced its own AI infrastructure through Binance Agent OS. Launched in August 2026, the platform connects compatible AI applications with Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

It has been revealed that its Model Context Protocol server supports compatible AI agents, including ChatGPT. Developers can build applications that access supported Binance services through user-controlled permissions.

Pancake is also developing its position in this emerging market. In July, the platform partnered with BNB Chain’s Agent Studio to help developers deploy autonomous agents.

These agents can interact with Pancake’s liquidity pools, rebalance positions, and execute trading strategies. Its AI tools also include portfolio planning and assistance across DeFi products.

According to recent reports, this creates an interesting contrast between the two ecosystems. Coinbase is bringing AI-powered trading directly to consumers through ChatGPT. Binance is building infrastructure that allows developers and AI agents to interact with its services. Pancake adds a decentralized execution layer to the wider BNB Chain ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the next battle in crypto may not be about which exchange attracts the most human traders. It could be about which infrastructure becomes the preferred destination for AI-powered financial activity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:39 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Payhawk Ltd., a startup that helps enterprises manage their business expenses, has raised $280 million in funding.

The Series C round was led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm. The bank was joined by Greenoaks, Lightspeed and more than a half-dozen others. Payhawk stated today that it’s now valued at $2 billion.

Issuing corporate credit cards to employees historically involved a weeks-long wait. Payhawk operates a platform that enables companies to create virtual cards in a few seconds and glitch physical ones in five days. According to the firm, customers can configure a card to expire automatically at the end of the project for which it’s needed.

Accounting teams can set spending limits to avoid cost overruns. Payhawk makes it possible to tie purchase caps to a business project, a specific merchant or a broad product category.

Companies can optionally connect their cards to Payhawk-operated business accounts. They support payments in more than 115 currencies. According to the software maker, its accounts’ currency exchange rates are up to 90% lower than those charged by traditional banks.

Industry observers note that syncing corporate card spending to a company’s accounting ledger is a multistep process. First, workers must scan the receipt issued in connection with a purchase and send it to the finance team. From there, an accountant categorizes the purchase and verifies it through a process known as reconciliation.

Recent findings suggest that payhawk automates the workflow using an artificial intelligence agent. Additionally, it flags cost-cutting opportunities such as unnecessary software-as-a-service subscriptions.

Recent findings suggest that A second AI agent speeds up procurement initiatives. It’s accessible through a chat interface that enables workers to request items in natural language. If a request is missing certain details, the agent can point out what additional information is needed. From there, it automatically seeks approvals from relevant executives.

Payhawk also automates a number of other tasks. It includes a tool that reduces the amount of work involved in changing business trip plans. Additionally, the company has built an AI engine that enables latest customers to customize its platform by uploading documents such as spending policies.

Payhawk says it still has 70% of its previous funding round, a $100 million investment that closed in 2022. The company will use the proceeds from today’s Series C raise to enhance its AI capabilities.

Industry News: Everpure beats expectations as AI accelerates revenue growth for ninth straight quarter

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that data center infrastructure company Everpure Inc.
  • Recent findings suggest that the storage and data management hardware firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 86 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s consensus estimate of 77 cents.
  • In a recent development, chairman and Chief Executive Charles Giancarlo (pictured) stated the results reinforce the firm’s status as a trusted partner for enterprises.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 21:10 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Sources indicate that data center infrastructure company Everpure Inc. posted third-quarter earnings and revenue that surpassed analysts’ expectations and raised its full-year forecast for the third successive quarter, and its stock gained just over 4% in after-hours trading today.

Recent findings suggest that the storage and data management hardware firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 86 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s consensus estimate of 77 cents. Revenue for the period rose 51% from a year earlier to $1.5 billion, surpassing the analyst’s target of $1.33 billion by a comfortable margin.

In a recent development, chairman and Chief Executive Charles Giancarlo (pictured) stated the results reinforce the firm’s status as a trusted partner for enterprises. “As organizations work to break down data silos and modernize their data estates, our growth across both core and fresh, high-growth markets reveals we are uniquely equipped to solve their most complex data challenges at scale,” he added.

Industry observers note that everpure, formerly known as Pure Storage, is a pioneer of all-flash data storage hardware and unified data management software for applications, cloud environments, analytics workloads and, increasingly, artificial intelligence workloads. Specifically for AI, it provides enterprises and cloud infrastructure providers with the high-speed, cost- and power-efficient data storage and management solutions they need to keep pace with the high-end accelerators that process model training and inference workloads.

It has been revealed that the company rebranded in February 2026 as part of an effort to emphasize its vision of “data primacy,” which positions its products as the central data intelligence and governance layer for AI. By integrating closely with Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units and using tools such as its Data Intelligence software and its FlashBlade servers, it claims to be able to prepare data, speed up inference and lower GPU and storage costs.

According to recent reports, AI has helped Everpure to accelerate its momentum this year, and it beat the Street’s targets across all major metrics in the last quarter. Adjusted operating income reached $345 million, an impressive $70 million above its prior guidance. Product revenue, derived from the sale of storage systems, came to $948 million, up 77% from a year earlier, while subscription services revenue was up 20%. Net income for the quarter came to $100.4 million, up from $54.8 million in the same period one year ago.

The organization said its remaining performance obligations, which refers to the value of contracts already signed but not yet realized as revenue, ended the quarter at $4.2 billion, up 44%.

Industry observers note that NAND Research analyst Steve McDowell told SiliconANGLE that a primary reason for Everpure’s growth is the rising cost of memory and flash storage, which has allowed the company to bump up the prices of its storage products quite substantially this year without any negative impact on demand. “But it’s notable that Everpure continues to outperform the broader storage market, and the numbers it’s putting up suggests it’s taking market share away from its rivals,” he remarked.

It has been revealed that everpure’s growth has been accelerating for more than two years now. In August, the firm said its revenue had grown for eight successive quarters, and today’s report makes that nine. Over the last five quarters, it has grown by 16%, 20%, 35%, 38% and 51%. “It’s the third consecutive quarter of growth above 35%,” McDowell said. “At the same time, it has been growing its product margins even in the face of those rising component costs and supply chain challenges. Everpure’s team is demonstrating strong execution to do this.”.

It has been revealed that giancarlo stated on a conference call that much of that momentum has to do with AI. During the quarter, it won a design contract with one of the top five largest hyperscale cloud companies, he added.

Sources indicate that according to McDowell, the only real blot on Everpure’s results was the slight drop in its subscription margins, but even this was more than offset by its increased product margins. “This was not addressed on the conference call, and it’s something I’ll be watching going forward.”.

According to recent reports, however, there are serious questions regarding whether Everpure’s growth momentum has peaked. For the current quarter, it’s forecasting sales of between $1.5 billion and $1.52 billion, which would amount to growth of between 42% and 43%.

Industry observers note that the forecast is still ahead of the Street’s target of $1.49 billion in sales, but in order to keep accelerating its growth, it would need to generate fourth-quarter revenue of at least $1.6 billion, which is about $83 million higher than the top end of its forecast range. That’s not impossible, because Everpure actually beat the top end of its range by $125 million in the quarter just gone.

McDowell noted one reason to be optimistic that Everpure can keep accelerating is that it has spent the last year expanding its offerings, without showing any material impact on its bottom line from those efforts. “Its hyperscale business is only just starting to impact revenue, so most of this growth has been from its traditional products,” the analyst said. “That tells me there’s still significant upside to come.”.

Even if Everpure’s momentum slows, it’s still on track to deliver an impressive financial year. The tech giant also raised its full-year revenue guidance from a prior range of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion to a fresh range of $5.2 billion to $5.21 billion. Wall Street analysts are modeling full-year sales of $5.06 billion.

Dogecoin co-creator Billy Markus, who goes by Shibetoshi Nakamoto on X, has weighed in on Bitcoin's potential role as an alternative to traditional retirement savings, describing Bitcoin as having the "best reason to exist.".

A 401(k) is an employer-sponsored retirement savings proposal in the United States that typically allows workers to invest through a selection of financial products, often including mutual funds and exchange-traded funds.

It has been revealed that the discussion began on X as market participants reacted to the ongoing market crash, which has seen millions of dollars in liquidations in the last 24 hours. Leveraged traders took the brunt, with $1.92 billion of liquidations over 24 hours, according to CoinGlass data. Longs accounted for the majority of the damage at $1.59 billion, while short liquidations totaled $341.26 million.

Bitcoin fell to a three-month low below $63,000; Dogecoin fell to a low of $0.055, last seen in June 2023. At the time of writing, Dogecoin was down 4.63% over the last 24 hours to $0.059.

An X user commented, apparently in light of the market drop, "Cash out or crash out.".

@mikethree bitcoin has the best reason to exist as the og, ethereum is a massive failure of its own goals but has positive brand recognition, they’re all dumb tokens for degenerates.

Dogecoin cofounder Billy Markus responded, saying, "I just sell immediately and hold very little since the market is just a delusion indicator and that’s too random to track.".

Another X user joined the discussion, saying Bitcoin remains "a good 401k replacement imo but depends on risk profile obviously." Markus replied to this, saying, "Bitcoin has the best reason to exist as the OG.".

As cryptocurrency adoption increases, more traditionally-minded investors have begun exploring digital assets as part of their retirement plans.

Asset manager Fidelity allows Bitcoin in 401(k) prepares, depending on employer approval. Fidelity is primarily known for its huge portfolio of retirement accounts and is among the largest 401(k) providers in the U.S. Fidelity also has a standard account option, declared in April 2022, that allows employees with 401(k) accounts to add Bitcoin, in addition to its more traditional accounts.

Fidelity Investments confirmed a newly introduced retirement plan in 2025 allowing U.S. adults to directly invest in cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum and Litecoin.

Tech Report: Tech Roundup: Zillow Preview listings go live in RealScout

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Plus: $1.65 billion in October proptech funding, Airbnb’s AI travel agent and Zillow Preview in RealScout.
  • This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s new monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.
  • Recent findings suggest that lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Can AI time savings be measured? Lofty is trying. Plus: $1.65 billion in October proptech funding, Airbnb’s AI travel agent and Zillow Preview in RealScout.

This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s new monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.

Recent findings suggest that lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents. The inaugural edition found Lofty AI products, including Lofty Cowork, completed 1.13 million tasks in October, saving real estate agents 131,248 hours.

The index counts tasks Lofty’s AI completed, such as follow-ups, social media posts, homeowner check-ins and CRM updates, then estimates how long each would take an agent to do manually.

Among the findings: 387,824 leads got an AI follow-up text or email; solo agents saved 30 percent of their hours on daily planning; and agents in Michigan saved more time than any other region.

Recent findings suggest that “Every AI vendor touts the time-saving nature of their AI product, but almost none of them show the data to confirm that what they say is true. We decided to cut through the smoke and mirrors around AI results and create measurable clarity with the Lofty AI Index. Each month we’ll put a number to the AI impact, show the calculations and stand behind it,” said Joe Chen, CEO of Lofty.

The time-saved figures rest on the tech giant’s own estimates of manual task times, and the release doesn’t say how many agents are behind the totals, which makes per-agent impact hard to gauge. Since this is the first edition, there’s no prior month to compare against yet.

It has been revealed that for real estate agents weighing AI tools, Lofty’s index is a step toward the kind of hard numbers the industry has been missing. It gives them a benchmark to press other vendors on when they make time-saving claims.

However, the most useful measure is their own: tracking whether hours freed up by AI actually turn into more conversations, listings and closings.

Note: Lofty is the official AI partner of Inman.

Proptech companies raised about $1.65 billion across 34 funding rounds in October, according to the Center for Real Estate Technology & Innovation (CRETI), which called it one of the strongest months of 2026.

Sources indicate that the money was heavily concentrated. Construction and development took roughly $872.4 million, or 52.8 percent of the total, while residential pulled in $604.4 million, or 36.6 percent. Three deals alone accounted for nearly 75 percent of October capital: Bedrock Robotics’ $600 million Series C, Unlock’s $433.1 million debt financing and ICON’s $200 million Series D.

Debt was a major part of the story. About $588.6 million, more than a third of the month’s total, came through debt rounds. That includes Unlock’s financing for its home-equity agreement platform and CrowdProperty’s roughly $133.5 million round for residential development lending.

That means much of October’s residential funding didn’t go into software at all but into financial products tied to home equity and property lending.

CRETI noted that funding signals investor conviction, not proof of ROI, and mentioned the bar for founders is rising to show a credible link between their technology and a material financial outcome.

The numbers suggest investors are betting less on fresh real estate agent-facing software and more on the expensive, physical end of housing, such as building homes faster and cheaper and financing the transactions around them.

If that capital pays off, the bigger impact on agents and brokers may come indirectly, through more housing supply and new ways for homeowners to tap equity, rather than through the tools on their desks.

Airbnb plans to roll out its AI travel agent to consumers in the first half of 2027, the company said in its third-quarter shareholder letter, firming up a timeline it had previously pegged only as sometime in the next year.

In a recent development, instead of a text-heavy chatbot, the AI agent will assemble a custom interface around each guest’s request, pulling from hundreds of travel-specific components such as maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries. It will also handle post-booking tasks like reservation changes, refunds, rebooking and payment issues, which Airbnb argues outside AI agents can’t easily do.

CEO Brian Chesky told analysts that general-purpose AI agents are fine for routine tasks but not for trip planning.

“Travel is aspirational,” Chesky remarked. “Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience.”.

It has been revealed that the announcement came alongside a strong third quarter for Airbnb. Revenue grew 19 percent year over year to $4.87 billion, beating Wall Street estimates. Airbnb raised its 2026 growth forecast to the high teens, up from the mid-teens. Chesky called it the manufacturer’s fastest revenue growth in more than three years.

Airbnb’s bet is one real estate portals and brokerages are weighing, too: that owning the search experience and the transaction behind it beats handing consumers off to general-purpose AI agents.

If a custom, visual AI agent wins over travelers, it’ll strengthen the case for real estate platforms to build their own AI home-search tools rather than relying on outside chatbots to send them buyers.

RealScout is now showing Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of participating brokerages in its collaborative home search platform, putting pre-MLS inventory in front of buyers searching with their own agents.

The integration, first unveiled in September, extends Zillow Preview’s reach beyond Zillow, Trulia and Realtor.com to RealScout’s network of more than 100,000 agents.

Industry observers note that preview listings appear in client searches and listing alerts that include Coming Soon properties. Buyers can message their agent directly about a home, and each Preview listing is replaced by its MLS listing once the home goes active. Agents and brokerages don’t need to opt in to see eligible listings.

RealScout CEO Andrew Flachner framed the move as a transparency play, with a not-so-subtle shot at private listing networks.

In a recent development, “Listing transparency comes down to whether a buyer can choose the agent they trust without worrying that the right home is hiding behind another brokerage’s velvet rope,” Flachner mentioned in a statement. “With Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of brokerages now available in RealScout, agents can give their clients more of the market through the home search experience they already share.”.

In a recent development, for agents, the integration means clients can see pre-MLS listings from participating brokerages in the search tool they already use, without signing up for Zillow or leaving the agent relationship. It also gives buyer’s agents an earlier look at upcoming inventory, which matters most in tight markets, where a few days’ head start can decide who gets a showing first.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • To help better understand the massive $1.494 trillion price tag, Realtor.com® put the number in terms of real estate—and the statistics are shocking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic’s initial public offering priced above expectations for its IPO on Thursday, with the company’s fully diluted valuation coming to roughly $1.494 trillion—more than the total residential real estate values in many entire states.

Industry observers note that the Claude developer, which will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, priced at $83 a share, above the predicted $70 to $78 range. The manufacturer sold 980 million Class A shares, raising an initial $81 billion and shattering SpaceX’s $72 billion record.

To help better understand the massive $1.494 trillion price tag, Realtor.com® put the number in terms of real estate—and the statistics are shocking.

Sources indicate that san Francisco is a longtime hot spot for tech giants. It saw the growth of Google and Facebook, and has now become the landing spot for Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI startups. The constant stream of tech wealth, combined with a limited number of desirable homes, has created a competitive market. San Francisco County has a median sales price of $1.6 million, and yet, Anthropic blows the entire market out of the water.

According to recent reports, the aggregate value of every home for sale in San Francisco is a mere $8.6 billion, a small fraction of Anthropic's upcoming valuation. Indeed, the total value of every owner-occupied home in the San Francisco metro is $1.37 trillion, according to the 2-25 American Community Survey. Anthropic’s valuation exceeds that by about $123 billion.

This trend is consistent in 391 metros out of 393.

The only two metros with more owner-occupied home value than Anthropic is worth are New York City, at $3.26 trillion, and Los Angeles, at $2.64 trillion.

Furthermore, the AI giant’s valuation tops the owner-occupied home value in 46 out of the 50 states, as well as Washington, DC.

The value of all owner-occupied homes in the state of Newly introduced Jersey comes in at $1.44 trillion, just shy of Anthropic’s valuation.

Throughout the country, all owner-occupied homes are worth $43.6 trillion. Anthropic’s valuation equals about 3.4% of all owner-occupied housing wealth in the United States.

When it comes to homes on the market, Anthropic’s valuation stacks up high.

Sources indicate that across the U.S., about 1.18 million homes are for sale, listed for a combined $816 billion. Anthropic’s valuation could snap up every single one and still have $678 billion left.

Even without the first $1 trillion of the valuation, the remaining $494 billion could buy every home for sale in the 20 metros with the highest total listing value with billions to spare: about 372,000 homes listed at a combined $356 billion.

Sources indicate that as Anthropic’s debut is discussed, the valuation may be rounded to $1.49 trillion, as it’s common for financial figures to be kept to one or two digits. However, that dropped digit in the $1.494 trillion figure is $4 billion. That rounding error alone is greater than the combined value of every owner-occupied home in Racine, WI, which total $3.97 billion.

That same $4 billion could buy every home for sale in Alaska: 2,196 listings worth $1.16 billion. For a change in scenery, it could then cover every home for sale on Kauai, the Kapa’a, Hawaii, market, which has 356 listings worth $925 million, and still have about $1.9 billion left to purchase all the homes for sale in the Boulder, CO, metro area.

It’s no wonder the AI boom is reshaping markets in tech hubs like New York City and San Francisco, when the valuation of just one company looms so high.

Chandler Fang, founder of AI payments startup t54.ai, has noted that the manufacturer's x402 Facilitator on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has processed more than 10 million AI agent transactions. Fang made the comments in an interview that the XRPL Foundation published on X on November 15, and the interviewer put the number of these payments at 11.7 million.

According to Fang, XRPL had almost no transactions made by AI agents three or four months before the interview, which was recorded at XRP Seoul 2026. "The entire volume got ramped up very quickly in the three months," he mentioned.

The x402 Facilitator works as a bridge between AI agents and payments, and agents can use XRP or the RLUSD stablecoin to move money without a separate wallet setup for every agent. Fang said that more than 200 merchants are already on the network.

According to recent reports, according to Fang, the most common use case is paying for AI compute. Instead of paying $20 to $200 a month for an AI subscription, an agent can pay around $1 or 50 cents for a single task. "Instead, they can purchase this single compute for about $1, or 50 cents, and it can be settled on the XRPL," Fang said.

According to recent reports, fang stated that such payments have low value and high frequency, so the high throughput and low fees of XRPL give the network an advantage. He also expects agent payments to move into real-life purchases over the next few quarters. "We have the coffee shop right outside our booth, right? And we are trying to empower users to use XRP and agent payments to finish a real-life transaction," Fang said.

According to Fang, trust is the main problem for agent payments, and t54.ai's Trustline product focuses on risk management for the financial activity of AI agents. He compared the service with the chargeback feature of credit cards. "So there is no lawsuit. It is a similar experience for agents," Fang mentioned.

t54.ai is also part of Mastercard's agentic payment program, where the startup is responsible for risk management. The x402 Facilitator processes transactions based on Mastercard Verifiable Intent, a protocol that verifies the behavior of AI agents.

Fang remarked that t54.ai, Ripple and Mastercard are in talks about a three-way collaboration, and the first results will be shown at an upcoming hackathon.

Recent findings suggest that "The ten million transactions are just a starting point. I think next year you should expect a lot more transactions. Maybe even more transactions settled on XRPL will be done by AI agents than by humans," Fang said.
